name: Knowledge-driven Zero-shot Learning
description: External knowledge (a.k.a. side information) plays a critical role in zero-shot learning (ZSL) which aims to predict with unseen classes that have never appeared in training data. Several kinds of external knowledge, such as text and attribute, have been widely investigated, but they alone are limited with incomplete semantics. Some very recent studies thus propose to use Knowledge Graph (KG) due to its high expressivity and compatibility for representing kinds of knowledge. However, the ZSL community is still in short of standard benchmarks for studying and comparing different external knowledge settings and different KG-based ZSL methods. In this paper, we proposed six resources covering three tasks, i.e., zero-shot image classification (ZS-IMGC), zero-shot relation extraction (ZS-RE), and zero-shot KG completion (ZS-KGC). evaluation_method: accuracy, F1, and ranking metrics such as MRR/hits@k depending on the task
typical_sota_score: varies by task; e.g., ZS-IMGC ≈70–85% (accuracy), ZS-RE ≈60–80% (F1), ZS-KGC ≈40–70% (MRR / hits@k)
reputation: A specialized benchmark for zero-shot learning with knowledge graphs that is useful in research but not broadly standardized.
notes: Covers multiple zero-shot tasks and knowledge settings, so scores are not directly comparable across resources; non-LLM benchmark and likely sensitive to dataset-specific splits.
